image.subject: A close photograph of a small stack of colored Sunday school tickets on a worn wooden schoolroom desk in a Missouri town, one ticket lifted between two fingers in the window light.

storyboard.claim: The town agreed on the tickets as value, but the agreement is hollow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Colored Sunday school tickets on a desk, one held up for inspection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the thesis that value is a shared agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tickets are the currency the agreement rests on.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, a grin that is half mischief, a tin bucket in hand, standing beside a whitewashed picket fence on a dusty board sidewalk in summer.

storyboard.claim: Tom uses the same trick on the fence and in the Sunday school, and decides to scale it up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom beside a whitewashed fence with a tin bucket, scheming grin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the fence-and-tickets economy into a bigger plan.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the whitewash labour to the Sunday school currency.

storyboard.claim: Tom decides to manipulate the town's emotions and his own existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only beat: the shock line lands on the words.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates from tickets and fences to his own life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the funeral as Tom's own production.

storyboard.claim: The next sequence is one of the most famous and twisted in the book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only transition into the funeral sequence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A signpost before the story turns to the funeral.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the book's most famous set piece.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn, a thin barefoot 13-year-old in ragged homespun clothes with a battered straw hat, sitting on a rough wooden raft tied to a willow on the Mississippi bank at dusk, the broad brown river and an island of willows ahead.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck run away with a third boy to Jackson's Island to be pirates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two boys on a raft tied to a willow at dusk, the island ahead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the funeral framing to the escape that causes it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the island and the boys' pirate plan.

image.subject: An empty raft drifting on the broad brown Mississippi at dawn, a torn shirt snagged on its rope and no one aboard, the willows of the island on the far bank.

storyboard.claim: The town finds a runaway raft and assumes the boys drowned.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty raft drifting on the river, a torn shirt snagged on its rope.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys vanish; the town reads the empty raft as death.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows how the town reached its false conclusion.

storyboard.claim: The boys learn they are presumed drowned, and Tom sees an opportunity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only question on screen.
storyboard.onScreenText: And what does Tom do with that?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The raft finding turns into a question about Tom's next move.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the viewer ask what Tom will do with his own death.

image.subject: A white wooden church steeple in a small Missouri river town on a still Sunday morning, dew on the grass and a whitewashed picket fence in the foreground, the street empty.

storyboard.claim: A still Sabbath morning with the church bell tolling instead of ringing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A white church steeple on a silent morning, empty street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question of Tom's plan moves to the town's mourning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes the solemn setting of the return.

image.subject: A stout grey-haired woman of about sixty in a black mourning dress and black veil, a grey-haired woman's hand on the arm of a neat 9-year-old boy in a pressed black suit, climbing the steps of a timber church in deep black.

storyboard.claim: Aunt Polly, Sid, Mary and the Harper family enter the church dressed in mourning black.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grieving aunt and a boy in black climbing church steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The town's mourning families arrive after the tolling bell.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Aunt Polly in grief before the reveal of her suffering.

image.subject: A timber church interior in the 1840s, townspeople in dark clothes rising from their pews while a grieving family walks slowly down the aisle, heads bowed, sunlight from high windows.

storyboard.claim: The whole congregation rises as the grieving families walk down the aisle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A congregation standing as a family walks down the aisle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The families' arrival becomes a communal rising.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the town's collective grief as one picture.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, peering down through the balusters of a church gallery at the weeping congregation below, a grin tugging at his mouth.

storyboard.claim: Tom and his pirate brothers have secretly returned from the island and watch from the church gallery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom peering from the gallery rail at the weeping pews below.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mourners below are unaware that the dead boys are above them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the viewer in the gallery with Tom.

image.subject: A dim dusty church gallery loft stacked with broken old benches and forgotten furniture, two boys crouched low among them, a thin shaft of light from a small window on the floorboards.

storyboard.claim: The boys hide in a chaos of invalid benches and dusty furniture in the gallery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cluttered gallery loft with two crouched boys.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the hiding place a physical clutter.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the boys are hidden among junk, not seated in pews.

storyboard.claim: The boys are watching their own funeral, a masterpiece of dramatic irony.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the irony.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the gallery hiding into the irony of the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the dramatic irony directly.

storyboard.claim: Society appreciates you most when you are entirely unavailable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the cynical truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the irony to a general truth about people.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the thesis about social value and absence.

image.subject: Aunt Polly, a stout grey-haired woman of about sixty in a dark dress with a white collar and spectacles on a cord, dabbing her eyes with a handkerchief in a church pew, a black-clad congregation around her.

storyboard.claim: Community sentiment is manipulated by making someone seem gone for good.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly weeping in a pew with a handkerchief.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The general truth now has a grieving face.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts Aunt Polly's grief on screen as the cost.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled sandy-haired 12-year-old boy, half-hidden in the shadows of a church gallery, a small satisfied grin on his face as he looks down at the town.

storyboard.claim: Tom discovers that his social stock rises as his value is measured by the town's grief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom in gallery shadow with a smug grin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the town's grief to Tom's own gain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom's satisfaction as a snapshot.

image.subject: A bare farmhouse kitchen wall with a hickory switch hung on a nail beside a stout woman's apron, a whitewash brush leaning on the floorboards below, morning light through the window.

storyboard.claim: Alive, Tom is a nuisance constantly whipped by Aunt Polly; dead, his value soars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A switch hanging on a kitchen wall, a whitewash brush on the floor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts Tom's life at home with his value as a ghost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the switch that marked his life before the disappearance.

image.subject: A small weathered wooden grave marker at the edge of a churchyard, fresh turned earth beside it and a few wilted flowers, a sunlit church wall behind.

storyboard.claim: Dead, Tom becomes a hero, and the validation he gets from the rafters is insane.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fresh grave marker in a churchyard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The alive-versus-dead contrast becomes a grave.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the death staging literal with a grave marker.

image.subject: A minister in a black coat at a wooden lectern in a timber church, one arm lifted, a Bible open before him, preaching to a sobbing congregation in the afternoon light.

storyboard.claim: The minister reframes every mischievous act as evidence of noble spirit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A minister preaching at a lectern to a tearful congregation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The shared grief gets a voice in the sermon.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the sermon as the town's reframing of the boys.

image.subject: A row of townspeople in dark clothes in a timber church, handkerchiefs at their eyes, all singing from open hymnals, faces lifted toward the rafters.

storyboard.claim: The congregation is sobbing as the minister calls for a hymn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sobbing townspeople singing from hymnals.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sermon leads into the singing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the hymn being sung by the mourners.

storyboard.claim: Old Hundred is a classic somber doxology hymn and a crucial detail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only naming of the hymn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the hymn the congregation is about to sing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies the hymn as a funeral doxology.

storyboard.claim: The hymn text praises God from whom all blessings flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation of the doxology line.
storyboard.onScreenText: Praise God from whom all blessings flow
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hymn's name is followed by its words.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the actual hymn lyric as a quotation.

image.subject: An open worn hymnal on a wooden lectern in a 19th-century Calvinist church, candlelight on its yellowed pages and the empty pews beyond.

storyboard.claim: Singing this hymn at a funeral seals the boys' permanence in the community's story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An open hymnal on a lectern in candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sung hymn becomes an object of finality.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the hymn as a sealed record.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn crouched in a dusty church gallery, Huck, a thin barefoot boy in a battered straw hat, staring down with an envious and watchful look while Tom turns to him, the hymn swelling below.

storyboard.claim: As the hymn swells, Tom looks at his envious friends Huck and Joe from the hiding spot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom and Huck in the gallery, Huck envious.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hymn's climax shifts the focus to the boys.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the friends who envy Tom's position.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a freckled sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, arms folded and chin up in the church gallery shadows, a window's light on his proud face.

storyboard.claim: Tom confesses in his heart that this is the proudest moment of his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom with folded arms and proud face in gallery shadow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the envious friends to Tom's own pride.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom's inner satisfaction as a physical posture.

image.subject: Sunlight across a timber church pew in which mourners sit weeping in black, and on the wall behind them the shadow of a boy leaning over the gallery rail.

storyboard.claim: Tom is soaking in the worship of the town, consuming its grief.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sunlit weeping pew with a boy's shadow on the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pride becomes a consumption of the town's sorrow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the grief as something Tom feeds on.

storyboard.claim: It is pure ego; Tom has achieved peak social value.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only punchline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the gallery sequence with a verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the moral verdict on Tom's ego.

image.subject: A quiet middle-aged man with a dark moustache in a dark suit and waistcoat, leaning on a writing desk with an open book, a half-smile on his face, the light of a window on the page.

storyboard.claim: It is hard to see the genius of the scheme while the morality of it disguises the view.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator at a writing desk with an open book.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The analysis turns to a critical voice, and the narrator's desk frames it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls the trading and gaming of the earlier chapters.

image.subject: Aunt Polly, a stout grey-haired woman in a black mourning dress with a white collar, alone in a dim kitchen with one hand pressed to her face and her spectacles in the other hand.

storyboard.claim: This crosses a serious line; Aunt Polly is genuinely suffering.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly alone in a dim kitchen, hand to her face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The analysis now has a face of the suffering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows her grief outside the church.

image.subject: A bedroom at night lit by one tallow candle, a stout grey-haired woman kneeling beside an empty bed with a patched quilt, her head bowed over her clasped hands.

storyboard.claim: Earlier, Aunt Polly wept by Tom's bed, believing he was dead, saying she had broken his heart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Aunt Polly kneeling beside an empty bed in candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The suffering is confirmed by an earlier scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the earlier grief at the bedside.

storyboard.claim: To let an old woman who loves you weep in a black dress just to feed your ego is not a childish prank.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the moral cost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The earlier grief is now a moral charge.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the act as a harm, not a prank.

image.subject: A black-gloved hand gripping a folded handkerchief on the rail of a timber church pew, the wood worn smooth and a single window's light across it.

storyboard.claim: Twain does not shy away from the immense pain this causes, and the act is borderline sociopathic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A black-gloved hand gripping a handkerchief on a pew rail.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The moral judgment is given a physical sign of grief.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pain as a gesture in place of gore.

image.subject: An empty wooden stage in a small riverside hall at dusk, a painted canvas backdrop of a forest, and a single candle in a tin lantern set on the boards.

storyboard.claim: To understand Tom, the actor-manager lens is needed: Tom as director of his own show.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty stage with a painted forest backdrop and one lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The moral judgment is reframed through theatre.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the stage metaphor.

storyboard.claim: To Tom it is theater, not malice: a play requires an audience and a tragedy requires tears.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only quotation of the theatre line.
storyboard.onScreenText: A play requires an audience. A tragedy requires tears.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stage metaphor becomes an explicit argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the logic of Tom's theatre.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, clinging to a single floating log on the dark brown Mississippi at dusk, his face set and determined.

storyboard.claim: Tom is so committed to the bit that he risked his life to make his return happen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom clinging to a single log on the dark river at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The theatre commitment is shown as physical risk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the crossing that the next beat explains.

image.subject: The wide dangerous Missouri shore at dusk, a single log drifting in dark water, the far bank a thin dark line and a steamboat's smoke on the horizon.

storyboard.claim: He paddled across the massive dangerous river on a single log at dusk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A single log drifting on a dark river at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The log from the last beat is set in its wide river.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the scale of the crossing.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer, a sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt, crouched behind the trunk of a tree in a dark wood at night, peering toward the lit window of a farmhouse.

storyboard.claim: Tom sneaks through the woods to secure his front-row seat to his own myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom crouched behind a tree, peering at a lit window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The crossing leads to the sneaking through the woods.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Tom watching the household as an audience.

storyboard.claim: Tom is the director, and the town does not know it is in a play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-only statement of the director idea.
storyboard.onScreenText: THEY DON'T KNOW THEY'RE IN THE PLAY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stage metaphor is named as direction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the play to the thesis about value.

image.subject: A crowd of townspeople in dark clothes gathered on the dusty street outside a timber church in the sunlight, all turned toward the steps, nodding in agreement with one another.

storyboard.claim: Tom forced the whole town to publicly agree on his irreplaceable worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd of townspeople outside a church, all nodding.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis returns with the whole town in agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the public agreement as a crowd.

image.subject: A sand-filled hourglass on a wooden windowsill with its last grains falling, the light of a dusky window across it and an empty room behind.

storyboard.claim: Tom manufactured the ultimate scarcity, death, to drive his value through the roof.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass with the last grains falling on a windowsill.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis closes on the image of scarcity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the scarcity of death a time-based symbol.
